draft.title: Protective factors for wellbeing
card: A protective factor is something that helps keep mental wellbeing high and lowers the chance of problems developing. It does not guarantee good mental health.
Biological factors include good food and enough sleep. They help the body and brain work well, which supports mood and concentration.

Psychological factors include coping strategies and mindfulness. Coping strategies are ways to deal with a stressful situation. Mindfulness is paying attention to the present moment without judging it.
Social factors include support from family, friends and community. Having people to turn to helps a person manage hard times.
draft.remember: Protective factors are habits, skills and supports that help keep wellbeing high.

a.q: Which of these is best described as a protective factor for mental wellbeing?
opts: Having friends and family to turn to in hard times
Being free of any stressful events in life
Having a mental health disorder diagnosed early
Avoiding all contact with other people when upset
a.why: Support from family and friends is a social protective factor because it helps a person manage hard times. Being free of stress is not what protective factors do: they help a person cope with it, and they do not remove it.
a.clue: Protective factors help a person manage problems, not remove them.

b.q: Priya is in Year 12 in Geelong. She sleeps eight hours most nights and uses breathing exercises when exams worry her. Which pair of protective factors does she show?
opts: A biological factor and a psychological factor
Two biological factors
A psychological factor and a social factor
A biological factor and a social factor
b.why: Enough sleep is a biological factor. Breathing exercises used to manage worry are a psychological coping or mindfulness strategy. No one else is involved in her routine, so no social factor is shown.
b.clue: Sort sleep and breathing exercises into the three types on the card.

a.best: Having friends and family to turn to in hard times

b.best: A biological factor and a psychological factor

problems.detail: The remember line regroups the factors as 'habits, skills and supports'. The card does not use these labels: it sorts the factors as biological, psychological and social. This tidier split could lead students to use non-syllabus categories.
